ATELIER — MONTRÉAL, QUÉBEC

The poetry
of metal.

Alu Romero hand-embosses sheet pewter into relief — sacred hearts, bodies, and quiet interiors, worked millimetre by millimetre from behind the metal.

SCROLL
Nothing here is cast, and nothing is printed. Every relief is pushed into being, one pass of the tool at a time.

SELECTED WORK

Fifteen pieces, one uninterrupted technique.

Each panel begins as a flat sheet of pewter. What follows is drawn out, not added on — figures, botanicals, and devotional forms raised entirely from within the metal.

THE TECHNIQUE

Repoussé — worked entirely from the reverse.

Repoussé is a metal ornamentation technique with roots stretching back thousands of years. The sheet is worked from behind: a hammer and a family of blunt tools coax the relief upward from the reverse side, while finer tools refine the detail from the front. Nothing is removed, and nothing is added — the image already exists inside the flat sheet, waiting to be pushed forward.

In Mexico, the technique has long lived in devotional metalwork — sacred hearts, milagros, and ex-voto offerings worked in tin and pewter. Alu Romero's atelier carries that lineage into a contemporary register: the same hand tools, turned toward the female form, botanicals, and reinterpretations drawn from art history, then set onto reclaimed wood, mirror, or frame for the wall.

Buril — traces and refines the finest linework
Perfilador — defines the outer edge of each form
Esfumino — softens and blends the raised surface
Reclaimed wood — the mount, for pieces made to live on a wall
THE ARTIST

Mexican hands, Montréal light.

Alu Romero is a Mexican artist living and working in Montréal. Her practice explores the poetry of metal through hand-embossed pewter — a slow, wholly manual technique she carries from Mexico's devotional metalworking tradition into large-scale contemporary pieces for the wall.

Her work moves between registers: sacred hearts and trees of life rendered with folk-art directness, quietly erotic studies of the body, and reinterpretations pulled from art history — all raised from the same flat sheet of pewter, by hand, from behind.

« Artiste mexicaine à Montréal. La poésie du métal à travers l'étain. »
